summary_paragraph: A female patient with systemic lupus erythematosus, antiphospholipid antibody syndrome, and end-stage renal disease on peritoneal dialysis was admitted after experiencing a seizure, severe headache, and visual disturbances. Initial evaluation revealed markedly elevated blood pressure, and MRI confirmed posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES), likely due to fluid overload. She underwent peritoneal dialysis, which normalized her blood pressure and resolved her neurological symptoms. Her home antihypertensive regimen was adjusted, discontinuing amlodipine and initiating verapamil and a low-dose metoprolol. Due to her history of PRES and use of bupropion, which can lower the seizure threshold, her bupropion dose was halved. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to monitor blood pressure closely and follow up with her nephrologist and psychiatrist.
problems: Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage V or end stage renal disease
Surgical operation with transplant of whole organ causing abnormal patient reaction, or later complication, without mention of misadventure at time of operation
